task.instruction: Read the latest health-related news article published on BBC News and summarize the key points discussed.

final_answer:
The most recent news article on BBC News' health index is **"Multi-million pound project to detect dementia"** (headline on the article page: "Exeter University-led £20m project to prevent and detect dementia"), published 14 hours ago — i.e. 7 November 2026 — by Chloe Parkman for BBC Devon.

**Key points:**

- **What it is:** A £20m research hub called BRAINIAC (AI and Emerging Technologies for Next Generation Brain Health Clinics), led by the University of Exeter. Half the money — £10m — comes from the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), part of UK Research and Innovation; the other £10m comes from industry, charity and NHS partners. It is one of five new hubs being funded across the UK.

- **What it will do:** Use AI to combine brain imaging, genetics, blood biomarkers and digital cognitive tests into a "single, clear picture of a person's brain health", with the aim of preventing and detecting dementia earlier. It brings together 11 universities — including Cambridge, Oxford, Newcastle, Swansea and Imperial College London — and 10 NHS sites, plus organisations such as Dementia UK and Alzheimer's Society, over a six-year project.

- **Clinics and timeline:** It will involve 10 brain health clinics across the UK, creating one of the biggest research platforms into what actually works to diagnose, prevent and treat dementia. The first clinics are due to start operating in 2029, initially open to people via NHS referral.

- **Targets:** The clinics aim to reduce risk and halve the time it takes to get a dementia diagnosis, make assessment and diagnosis 30% to 50% faster, and identify more than 40% of the people it assesses as at early risk — before symptoms develop. Separately, UKRI has committed up to £80m for researchers to develop tools that could support diagnosing 92% of people referred with suspected dementia within 18 weeks by 2029.

- **Why it matters:** About 982,000 people in the UK live with dementia, a figure set to reach 1.4m by 2040, with the annual cost more than doubling to £90bn. Director David Llewellyn, professor of clinical epidemiology and digital health, said detection was the "hardest problem", and that the tools built in NHS clinics would let clinicians "pick up the first signs before symptoms show" and offer a personalised prevention plan. Deputy director Chris Fox, professor of clinical psychiatry, said current treatments only help if people are diagnosed early, and that BRAINIAC would give the NHS the tools to do that "at scale", designed with patients and clinicians from the start "so they work in a busy clinic and not just on paper".

- **Context:** Professor Charlotte Deane, executive chair of the EPSRC at UKRI, said the five hubs build on previous ones already translating research into real benefits, including the world's first AI-assisted brain tumour surgery.

(Note: the health index's other recent items are "AI to help eye tests detect diabetes" and "Under-16s could be banned from buying energy drinks in Wales", both 1 day old, so the dementia story is the newest.)

judge.rationale: The agent opened the BBC Health page, selected the timestamped dementia news article, read its BBC text, and summarized its key points accurately.
